<a id="languagevoicelengths"></a>

## `LanguageVoiceLengths`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Voice.LanguageVoiceLengths` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

How a language set's clips compare in length with the game's own clips of the same name - the number that tells whether a translated take will change a scene's pacing.

The game waits for the clip that plays (story text rows wait for the text and the voice), so a longer take never gets cut; it makes the scene slower, and it shifts the few effects the game times by the clock (screen effects started with a fixed delay, the 20 s game-start cap). The window [`LanguageVoiceLengths.ShorterRatio`](#languagevoicelengths--shorterratio)..[`LanguageVoiceLengths.LongerRatio`](#languagevoicelengths--longerratio) is the one the voice pipeline aims for outside cutscenes.

<a id="languagevoiceplan"></a>

## `LanguageVoicePlan`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Voice.LanguageVoicePlan` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The language-scoped voice sets the loaded packs ship: `audio/voice/<lang>/<VoiceName>.ogg` (or `.wav`), decided from the pack indexes alone.

A file directly in `audio/voice/` is a global override ([`VoiceLoadPlan`](#voiceloadplan)) and is never part of a language set; [`PackContentIndex`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#packcontentindex) classifies a file one folder deeper as [`PackContentKind.Other`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#packcontentkind--other), so the global preload never sees it. This plan reads exactly those files, from [`PackContentIndex.Files`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#packcontentindex--files).

The folder name is a language code in any spelling [`SubtitleLanguages.Normalize`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Subtitles.md#subtitlelanguages--normalize) accepts (`th`, `TH`, `thai` are one set). Whether the code names a language this session can display is not decided here: the plan is built before the language registry, and an unknown code simply never becomes the active language.

Within one language the rules match [`VoiceLoadPlan`](#voiceloadplan): later pack over earlier pack, and within one pack the later path (ordinal) wins; every loser becomes a [`VoiceLoadSkip`](#voiceloadskip) naming its winner, so the outcome never depends on load timing.

The longest folder name accepted as a language code.

<a id="languagevoicerules"></a>

## `LanguageVoiceRules`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Voice.LanguageVoiceRules` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The precedence between the three kinds of override a voice name can have.

Most specific wins, and a mod's explicit choice wins over files on disk:

1. a runtime registration (a mod, e.g. a line a mod generated);
2. the language set of the language in force, when its clip is loaded;
3. a global pack clip;
4. the game's own clip.

A language clip that is still loading or failed is skipped for that one play - the line is never silent - which is why the language step needs the clip to be loaded, not merely planned.

<a id="languagevoicerules--askslanguageset"></a>

### `static bool AsksLanguageSet(VoiceEntry registered)`

True when the language set should be asked at all: a runtime registration answers before it, so asking would only produce a misleading fallback trace and a needless load.

**Parameters**

- `registered`: What the global registry holds for the name, or null.

<a id="languagevoicerules--choose"></a>

### `static VoiceChoice Choose(VoiceEntry registered, LanguageVoiceLookup language)`

Chooses who answers a lookup.

**Parameters**

- `registered`: What the global registry holds for the name, or null.
- `language`: What the language set of the language in force says.

<a id="languagevoiceswitch"></a>

## `LanguageVoiceSwitch`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Voice.LanguageVoiceSwitch` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Turns "the game's language is now X" observations into set changes: which language set is in force, and when that changes.

The language in force has a set only when a pack ships `audio/voice/<code>/` for it; any other language means "no set" (the game's own clips, plus global overrides). So a switch from Japanese to English is no change here, while Thai to English leaves the Thai set. Observing the same language again is cheap and reports nothing, so callers may observe on every voice lookup and on a timer.

<a id="languagevoicetable"></a>

## `LanguageVoiceTable`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Voice.LanguageVoiceTable` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The runtime state of every language set: which clips are waiting, loading, loaded or failed, the load order, and the lookup the voice prefix asks on every line.

Unity-free so the selection and scheduling rules are unit-tested: a clip is held as `Object` (a `UnityEngine.AudioClip` at runtime) exactly like [`VoiceEntry.Clip`](#voiceentry--clip).

Load order, per language: names asked for "now" first ([`LanguageVoiceTable.Prioritize`](#languagevoicetable--prioritize-string-string): a line that just fell back, or the lines of a scenario that is about to play), most recent request first; then, only when the caller allows background work, the rest in plan order. A failed clip is not retried automatically, so a broken file cannot become a load loop.

Every member takes the same lock; in practice everything runs on Unity's main thread.

**Parameters**

<a id="voiceloadplan"></a>

## `VoiceLoadPlan`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Voice.VoiceLoadPlan` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What a preload run will do, decided from the pack indexes alone: which files, in which order, through which loader, and which files are skipped with what reason.

Split out of the plugin so the conventions - name from file name, loader from extension, later packs override earlier ones - are unit-testable without Unity, and so the log line and the smoke detail cannot disagree with what was actually attempted.

Steps keep the order the packs were given in and, within a pack, the order of the index (ordinal by path). When two files would claim the same voice name - two packs shipping `Voice_A.ogg`, or one pack shipping both `Voice_A.ogg` and `Voice_A.wav` - only the last one is planned and the earlier ones become [`VoiceLoadPlan.Skipped`](#voiceloadplan--skipped) entries saying who overrode them. That is decided here rather than left to the registry on purpose: a WAV loads synchronously and an Ogg several frames later, so "whoever registers last wins" would otherwise make the winner depend on decode timing instead of on load order.

<a id="voicenamerules"></a>

## `VoiceNameRules`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Voice.VoiceNameRules` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What counts as a voice name, and how one is derived from a file name or from the path the game hands to its audio manager.

The character rule is deliberately narrow. A voice name ends up as a dictionary key that the game, our packs and a mod all spell independently, and the game's own names are plain ASCII (`Voice_Tutorial_1_001`). Allowing spaces, dots or non-ASCII would mean a clip that silently never resolves because one side normalised it and the other did not.

[`VoiceNameRules.KeyFromAudioPath`](#voicenamerules--keyfromaudiopath) mirrors `AudioManager<T>.PathToName` (KanKikuchi.AudioManager), which is `Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension` - the same call, so the two cannot drift apart.

<a id="voicenamerules--characterrulereason"></a>

### `const string CharacterRuleReason = "a voice name may only contain letters, digits, '_', '-' and parentheses (^[A-Za-z0-9_\\-()]+$)"`

Why a name was refused, when it is refused for its characters.

<a id="voicenamerules--pattern"></a>

### `const string Pattern = "^[A-Za-z0-9_\\-()]+$"`

The rule, as a regular expression, for documentation and error messages.

[`VoiceNameRules.IsValid`](#voicenamerules--isvalid) implements this as a character loop rather than a `Regex`: it runs inside a Harmony prefix on every clip lookup the game makes.

<a id="voicenamerules--isvalid"></a>

### `static bool IsValid(string name)`

True when `name` is a usable voice name.

**Parameters**

- `name`: The candidate name; null and blank are never valid.

<a id="voicenamerules--keyfromaudiopath"></a>

### `static string KeyFromAudioPath(string audioPath)`

The cache key the game would compute for an audio path, so a lookup can be answered with exactly the name the game itself would have used.

**Parameters**

- `audioPath`: What the game passed to `Play` - usually a bare name.

**Returns:** The key, or null when the path yields none.

<a id="voicenamerules--tryfromfilename"></a>

### `static bool TryFromFileName(string fileName, out string name, out string reason)`

Derives the voice name from a pack file name: the file name without its extension.

**Parameters**

- `fileName`: A file name such as `Voice_CWY_Test.wav`. A leading directory is tolerated and dropped, so a pack-relative path works too.
- `name`: The derived name, or null when there is none.
- `reason`: Why it was refused, or null on success.

**Returns:** True when a valid name was derived.

<a id="voiceregistry"></a>

## `VoiceRegistry`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Voice.VoiceRegistry` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Name to clip, with the rules that decide who wins when two registrations claim one name.

The rules, in full:

- A free name is taken by whoever asks first.
- Pack over pack: the later registration wins, which makes a pack loaded after another override it - the pack list is already in dependency order.
- Runtime over pack: a clip a mod registered outranks a file on disk, so a rescan of the packs never silently swallows a line a mod just generated. A caller that would rather defer to a pack passes `keepPack`.
- Runtime over runtime: the later registration wins; two mods claiming one name is last-one-in, and the log line says who displaced whom.

Names are matched with `StringComparer.Ordinal` - case-sensitively - because the game's own cache is an ordinary `Dictionary<string, AudioClip>` (KanKikuchi's `AudioManager`) and a name that differs only in case is a different clip there too.

Every member takes the same lock: packs preload on the main thread while a mod may register from a callback, and both touch this table.
